title: Add layout.align_lines next to center_lines
prompt:
The package layout in the current directory has `center_lines(text, width)` (layout/lines.py). Add, next to it,

    align_lines(text, width, align="center", fill=" ")

and export it from the package (`from layout import align_lines`). Behaviour:
- `text` is split on "\n"; every line first loses its trailing spaces and tabs, then is aligned in `width` columns with the one-character `fill`: "left" as str.ljust, "right" as str.rjust, "center" exactly as str.center does it. Lines that are already `width` or longer are kept as they are.
- width=None means the length of the longest line (after the stripping).
- The lines are joined with "\n" (no trailing newline is added; a text ending in "\n" therefore ends with an aligned empty line).
- ValueError when `align` is not one of the three names, when `fill` is not exactly one character, or when `width` is negative.

`center_lines` and `pad_cell` must keep their current behaviour. tests/test_lines.py has a few examples (run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`); a hidden suite checks the full behaviour. Do not modify tests/test_lines.py.
